name: context-trim
description: Pack a whole project into lean Markdown context: no lockfiles, build output, caches or binaries, credential files left out and API keys masked.

interface.shortDescription: Lean codebase context without lockfiles or secrets
interface.longDescription: context-trim packs a whole project into one Markdown document for the model. It leaves out lockfiles, build output, caches and binaries, never reads credential files such as .env or private keys, and masks API keys and passwords found in code. It is read-only: it never writes, deletes or sends anything, and it only reads folders inside your workspace. Use it to review, explain or summarize a codebase in one step, or to check how many tokens a project costs before you pack it.
defaultPrompt: Give me an overview of this codebase
How many tokens would this project cost to send?

positive.description: Packs the open project for a whole-codebase overview
positive.prompt: Give me an overview of this codebase and how its parts fit together.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks the token cost first, then packs the project and explains its structure from the packed files.

positive.description: Reports token cost and heaviest files
positive.prompt: How many tokens would it cost to send this whole project to you, and which files are the biggest?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns total tokens, the number of filtered files and the 10 heaviest files.

positive.prompt: Review the code in the src folder for bugs.
positive.expected_behavior: Packs the src folder only (path set to src) and reviews it.

positive.prompt: Summarize this repository, but keep the context under 10,000 tokens.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the tool with budget 10000; files past the budget are listed by name only and the answer says which were left out.

positive.description: Keeps secrets out of the context
positive.prompt: Pack this project so I can paste it into another chat. Make sure no API keys are included.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the pack with .env and key files left out and any keys in code shown as [REDACTED_SECRET_KEY].

negative.description: Single-file question does not need the whole project
negative.prompt: What does the function on line 12 of utils.js do?

negative.description: General programming question with no project involved
negative.prompt: What is the difference between let and const in JavaScript?

negative.description: Request to write or change files
negative.prompt: Create a new README file for my project.

publication.release_notes: First directory release: lean codebase packing with credential files left out, API keys masked, workspace-only access and a 20,000-token default budget.
